title.en: The Tang Monk and the River

halves.english_text: E104 : Journey to the West ( The Tang Monk and walk[wɔː k] road[rəʊd] field[fiːld] flower [ˈflaʊə(r)] look[lʊk] huge[hjuːdʒ] mountain[ˈmaʊntən] shake[ʃeɪk] easy[ˈiːzi] climb[klaɪm] laugh[lɑːf] ask[ɑːsk] Wukong and his companions walked through the Western Paradise . The road weaved through a field of flowers and toward the Spirit Mountain Bajie looked up at the huge mountain and shook his head. "It won't be easy to climb that." Wukong laughed . "Don't ask me to carry you!" The travelers soon arrived at a river with a strong current . Waves crashed into jagged rocks, spraying water everywhere "This river looks dangerous ," said Wujing. "But we must cross it to get to the Spirit Mountain Bajie sighed . "We will never be able to cross this river safely . Let's just go home "Nonsense ," said Wukong. "Look over there The monkey pointed upstream . A thin log lay across the river . It wobbled and shook as the water rushed under it. The Tang Monk looked at the log . "Don't be silly Wukong. We can't walk across that log—it's too thin . And it looks quite slippery "But that log is the only way to reach the Spirit Mountain," said Wukong. "You must believe that it's safe . Watch me!" The monkey hopped onto the log and ran across the river and back. "See ?" he said. "It's safe Bajie snorted. "You don't weigh much , Wukong. But if I step on that log, it will break "I believe Wukong," said Wujing. "We must walk across the log "Follow me, Master ," said Wukong. He pulled the Tang Monk toward the log The monk trembled with fear . "Don't make me walk across that! I'll fall into the river and drown "Let's just fly over the river," suggested Bajie. " We can carry Master and the horse." "No," insisted Wukong. "The Tang Monk must make the entire journey by himself. We're here to protect him, not to carry him. Buddha won't allow Master to have the True Scriptures if he doesn't take every step himself." Just then an old man appeared in a boat . "I can take you across the river," said the man.
halves.chinese_text: 悟空和他的同伴们在西天极乐世界中前行。道路蜿蜒穿过一片花海,朝着灵 山延伸而去。 八戒抬头望着那座巍峨的大山,摇了摇头说:“要爬上那座山可不容 易。”悟空笑道:“别指望我背你!” 实地 发抖 悟空 伙伴 走 西方极乐世界 道路 编织 田野 花朵 灵山 看 巨大的 山 摇动 容易的 爬 笑,发笑 问,询问 携带,搬运 旅行者 到达 河流 强烈的 水流 波浪 撞击 锯齿状的,不规则的 没一会儿,众人来到一条水流湍急的河边。波浪拍打着嶙峋的礁石,水花四 溅。 悟净说:“这条河看起来很危险,但我们必须得渡过它才能到达灵山。” 八戒叹了口气说:“我们根本不可能安全地渡过这条河。咱们还是回家 吧。” “别胡说,” 悟空说,“看那边。” 悟空指着上游。只见一根细细的原木横亘在河上。河水从下面奔腾而过,原 木摇晃不止。 唐僧看着那根原木说:“别犯傻了,悟空。我们不可能从那根原木上走过去 —— 它太细了,而且看起来很滑。” 喷洒,喷射 水 到处,处处 危险的 穿越 灵山 叹息,叹气 能够,能 穿越,横过 安全地,平安地 去,离开 家,房屋 废话 看 在那里 猴子 指向 上游 细的 木头 穿过 河 摇晃 摇动 冲,急速移动 原木;木头 傻的;愚蠢的 薄的;瘦的 滑的;不稳固的 “但那根原木是到达灵山的唯一途径,” 悟空说,“您得相信它是安全 悟空跳到原木上,从河这边跑到对岸,又跑了回来。“瞧见没?” 他 八戒哼了一声说:“你体重轻,悟空。可要是我踩上去,这原木肯定会 悟净说:“我相信悟空。我们必须从这根原木上走过去。” “师父,跟我来。” 悟空说着,拉着唐僧朝原木走去。 木头 方式 到达 相信 安全的 猴子 跳跃 到......上 跑 穿过 河流 看 安全的 称重 很多 打破 相信 走过 原木 大师 拉,拖 木头,原木 僧侣 颤抖 害怕 使,让 走,步行 穿过 摔倒 河 淹死 唐僧吓得浑身发抖。“别逼我从那上面走!我会掉进河里淹死的!” 八戒提议道:“咱们直接飞过去得了。我们可以带着师父和马。” “不行,” 悟空坚持道,“唐僧必须靠自己完成这整个旅程。我们在这里 是保护他,而不是背着他走。如果师父不是自己一步步走到的,佛祖不会把 就在这时,一位老人划船出现了。老人说:“我可以把你们送过河。” 飞 坚持 旅行 保护 搬运 允许 经典 人 出现 船 拿,带 穿过

halves.english_text: E104 : Journey to the West ( The Tang Monk and walk[wɔː k] across[əˈkrɒs] wrong[rɒŋ] bottom[bɒtəm] through[θruː] boat [bəʊt] safe[seɪf] climb[klaɪm] wait [weɪt] step[step] horse[hɔː(r)s] "Thank you," said the Tang Monk . He walked to the riverbank . "My companion wanted me to walk across that log, but—" The monk gasped "There's something wrong with your boat," he said to the man. "It has no bottom ! Water is flowing right through it!" "The boat is safe ," said the man. "Please climb in. Buddha is waiting With a bit more hesitation , the Tang Monk stepped into the boat . He was shocked to find that he didn't sink . He sat on the edge of the boat as Wujing led the horse aboard . Bajie and Wukong followed. The boat glided swiftly across the river . Suddenly there was a splash The Tang Monk looked at the water and saw a body floating downstream . He screamed . "A man has drowned Wukong put his hand on the monk's shoulder and smiled . "It's you, Master ." "What?" said the monk . "Me?" "Wukong is right !" cried Bajie . "It is you "Look again , Master," said Wujing, smiling. The Tang Monk looked at the body more carefully . It was wearing the same Buddhist robe that he was wearing. "It is me," said the monk quietly. " But how . . . ?" "You got rid of your mortal body, Master," said Wukong. "You're a spirit now." "You're one of us !" Bajie beamed. The boat soon reached the other riverbank, and the travelers stepped out. As they walked up the slope of the Spirit Mountain, the Tang Monk laughed in amazement. "I feel so light !" he said. "I feel like I could run right up this mountain "Good ," said Bajie. "Perhaps you could carry me Everybody laughed as they continued up the mountain.
